_note: Discovery album (P4). Each card: a real NASA photo (src/assets/cards/<id>.jpg, from images.nasa.gov) and one fact. The fact is either taken from the photo's own NASA caption (fact + link) or is an OSDR fact from facts.json (factId). Texts only say what the source page says (checked 2026-11-15).

cards.title: Layered rock
cards.fact: The Curiosity rover found finely layered rocks on Mount Sharp. The layers show that wind once piled this sand into moving dunes.

photo.alt: Layered rocks of the Murray Buttes on Mars, seen by Curiosity

cards.title: Blue sunset
cards.fact: On Mars, sunsets look blue! Fine dust in the air lets blue light through near the Sun. Curiosity took this photo on April 15, 2015.

photo.alt: A blue sunset over the hills of Gale Crater on Mars

cards.title: Morning frost
cards.fact: The Phoenix lander dug a trench in the Martian ground and saw frost in it one morning, on its 113th Martian day.

photo.alt: Pale frost inside a trench dug by the Phoenix lander

cards.title: Dust devil
cards.fact: Dust devils are little whirlwinds on Mars. They have blown dust off the solar panels of the rovers Spirit and Opportunity and given them more power.

photo.alt: A dust devil seen from above as a white puff over red hills

cards.title: Space radishes
cards.fact: In 2020, astronaut Kate Rubins grew radishes on the Space Station. The experiment studies how plants grow in space and how they taste.

photo.alt: Astronaut Kate Rubins checks radish plants growing on the Space Station

cards.title: Storm watcher
cards.fact: This is a real X-class solar flare, seen by NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory on March 29, 2014. Solar flares are powerful bursts of radiation.

photo.alt: A bright solar flare bursting from the glowing surface of the Sun

cards.title: Hello, Earth
cards.fact: This is Earth and its Moon, photographed from Mars on November 20, 2016. The Moon is much darker than Earth, so it was made brighter to see it.

photo.alt: Earth and the Moon as two small dots on black space, seen from Mars
Astronaut Drew Feustel checks on mice inside a glovebox on the Space Station

cards.title: Dust storm
cards.fact: In June 2018, a huge dust storm grew on Mars and covered the Opportunity rover. Dust storms like this can last weeks or even months.

photo.alt: Map of Mars with a big dust storm spreading over it

cards.title: Sun in the way
cards.fact: About every 26 months, Mars passes almost directly behind the Sun as seen from Earth. This is called solar conjunction.

photo.alt: Diagram: the Sun sits between Earth and Mars on their orbits

cards.title: Gale Crater
cards.fact: NASA's Curiosity rover landed in Gale Crater in August 2012. A tall mountain, Mount Sharp, rises in the middle of the crater. Curiosity's RAD instrument measured the everyday Mars radiation dose that this game uses.

photo.alt: Gale Crater seen from orbit, with a mountain in its middle

cards.title: Jezero Crater
cards.fact: NASA's Perseverance rover landed in Jezero Crater on February 18, 2021. Long ago a lake filled this crater, and a river left a fan-shaped delta. Old lake rocks are a good place to look for signs of ancient life.

photo.alt: Jezero Crater from orbit, with a circle marking Perseverance's landing area next to the old river delta

cards.title: Ice of Utopia
cards.fact: Under the ground of Utopia Planitia, the radar of NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter found a huge layer of water ice. It holds about as much water as Lake Superior, one of the biggest lakes on Earth.

photo.alt: Map of Utopia Planitia with stripes where radar found ice under the ground

cards.title: Hellas Basin
cards.fact: Hellas is one of the biggest impact craters in the solar system. It is so deep that the air at its bottom is the thickest on Mars, and thicker air blocks a little more radiation.

photo.alt: A colored height map of the huge, round Hellas Basin

cards.title: Moon over the Sun
cards.fact: In 2022, Perseverance filmed Phobos, one of the two moons of Mars, passing in front of the Sun. Watching these eclipses helps scientists measure how Phobos' orbit slowly changes.

photo.alt: The lumpy moon Phobos as a dark shape in front of the Sun

cards.title: Space rock
cards.fact: In January 2023, Curiosity found an iron-nickel meteorite nicknamed 'Cacao', about 30 centimeters across. It is a rock that fell onto Mars from space.

photo.alt: A dark, shiny metal rock sitting on pale Martian ground

cards.title: Shining clouds
cards.fact: In January 2025, Curiosity filmed glowing twilight clouds. Some of them are made of frozen carbon dioxide, or dry ice, and float 60 to 80 kilometers above the ground.

photo.alt: Thin, glowing clouds drifting in the evening sky of Mars
